hook.say: So if someone did not keep a promise in your house, it's *not* your *fault.* | Just look at the Father who is never late.

cues.text: But when **the fulness of the time** was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.
And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, **Abba, Father.**
Three truths for every child who has waited
God chose the hour — | and *He kept it.*
God did not | send excuses. | *He sent His Son.*
It wasn't *your job* | to get the money, | to make the peace.

cues.label: TRUTH 2 OF 3
cues.title: The Father Sent His Son, *Right On Time*

cues.text: Every waiting child, | every failed father, | could call Him *Father.*

cues.title: TODAY'S THREE TRUTHS
items: Grown-up problems are not your fault
The Father sent His Son, right on time
Come back to the Father first

cues.text: Every promise | He made to you | *will never fail.*

child.text: Write one promise you are still waiting for. Under it, write: “My Father in heaven is never late.” Keep it somewhere safe.

father.text: Write your child’s age now, and their age when you stopped being there. Look at the gap. Make no big promise yet. Pray for your child by name.

lines.text: Father, we pray for every son, every daughter listening, and every father,
that just like You are a reflection of the true Father, our fathers will reflect true fatherhood,
and our sons will see You as a Father who is never late.
Thank You, Jesus. In the name of Jesus Christ we pray. Amen.

art.prompt: Night inside a small one-room home with deep teal walls. In the foreground on the right, a small boy of about seven in a yellow shirt sits on a woven mat on the floor beside a single candle, hugging his knees, looking up toward a window where soft golden light is beginning to pour in onto his face. Far behind him on the left, small and out of focus, his mother sits at a wooden table with her head in her hand beside a few papers and an empty cooking pot. The boy is the clear subject and is gently lit; the mood is tender, he is not alone.

Night in a small West African village of round mud huts with thatched roofs. In the foreground on the left, seen from behind, a child wrapped in a patterned cloth sits on the stone doorstep of a hut beside a glowing oil lantern, hugging their knees, looking down the empty earth road. Far down the road a simple wooden stable glows with warm golden light from a manger inside, and one bright star hangs directly above it in a deep teal sky.

Night. A West African father in a green patterned shirt kneels alone on the floor of a small room with deep teal walls, head bowed, hands open on his knees, a steel wristwatch on his wrist. Behind him a wooden door stands open and warm golden light pours through it across the floor and over his shoulders, like someone is waiting for him in the light. A single candle burns on a small table; a child's crayon drawing of a family is pinned to the wall. He is on the left third of the frame; large calm empty area on the right filled with the soft light from the door, for titles.

social.description:
Some homes are full of big promises and very little money. Tonight we meet a Father who chose the hour and kept it: He sent His Son, right on time.

THE WORD: Galatians 4:4–5 (read Galatians 4:1–7 aloud)
TONIGHT, children: write one promise you are still waiting for. Under it, write: “My Father in heaven is never late.” Keep it somewhere safe.
TONIGHT, fathers: write your child’s age now, and their age when you stopped being there. Look at the gap. Make no big promise yet. Pray for your child by name.
SAY IT: My Father in heaven is never late.
